transcript.content: Hello, welcome. What brings you in to see me today?
I've been feeling low for a long time. I still do my routes and volunteer work, but most days there's this heavy feeling, like I'm just going through the motions instead of really living my life.
When you say you've been feeling this way for a long time, about how many months or years has it been?
About three years now—since my father died.
During these past three years, have there been any times when your mood lifted and felt completely normal for more than two months?
No, I can't say it's felt completely normal for that long. It's been about three years since my father died, and it's mostly stayed with me.
Before your father passed away three years ago, had you ever had periods in your life when you felt depressed or down like this?
I’m not really sure. I can’t think of a period before that where I felt down like I do now.
During this time, have you had thoughts of death, or felt like life isn't worth living?
I’m not sure what you mean exactly. I do know I’ve felt low for a long time, but I haven’t really thought about it in those terms.
Have you lost interest or pleasure in the things you used to enjoy?
I’m not sure. I haven’t really noticed a clear change in that, to be honest.
Have you been feeling unusually tired or lacking energy most days?

I’m still getting to work and helping at the pantry, but it takes more pushing than it used to. I’ve got this application for a logistics supervisor job just sitting unfinished—I don’t really trust myself to keep up with it.
How has your sleep been over these past few years?

Mostly before a run, I have trouble sleeping. I’ll lie there thinking about all the stops the next day, or I wake up around four and can’t really get back to sleep. I still get to work on time, but I feel worn down before the day even starts.
Have you noticed any changes in your appetite or weight over these past few years?
I haven’t really noticed any big change in my appetite or weight.
